explain.say: Look around your home. Which machine do you think gulps electricity fastest: the TV, the fridge, the phone charger or the kettle? Most people guess the TV. Let us line them up by power, which means how fast they use energy.

explain.say: Look at the tallest bar: the kettle, about 3000 watts! A watt is one joule of energy every second. Anything that heats things, like kettles, hair dryers and irons, needs lots of power. Which bar comes second?

explain.say: The hair dryer, 2000 watts, yes! Now look way down: the TV is about 100 watts, the LED bulb only 10, and the phone charger about 5. The kettle is 300 times hungrier than the LED bulb. Did you guess right?

items.label: LED bulb
items.ask: Why do LED bulbs use so little power?

explain.say: But power is only half the story. Energy used equals power times time. The kettle at 3 kilowatts for 3 minutes uses 0.15 kilowatt-hours. An LED bulb left on for 15 hours uses exactly the same! So what matters too?

explain.say: How long things are on, well done! Bills are measured in kilowatt-hours, called units. Wow fact: in the UK, TV ad breaks once caused millions of kettles to switch on together, so power stations had to be ready for the surge. Challenge: check the watts printed on your phone charger.

faq.q: Which appliance uses the most power?
faq.a: Heating appliances such as kettles, electric showers, ovens and hair dryers have the highest power ratings, often 2000 watts or more.
asks: Which appliance uses the most electricity?

faq.q: Why do LED bulbs use so little power?
faq.a: LEDs turn most of their energy into light instead of heat, so they need only about a tenth of the power of old filament bulbs.

faq.q: How do you work out energy used by an appliance?
faq.a: Multiply power in kilowatts by time in hours to get kilowatt-hours. A 2 kilowatt heater for 3 hours uses 6 kilowatt-hours.
A kilowatt-hour is the energy used by a 1000 watt appliance running for one hour. Electricity bills charge per kilowatt-hour.
asks: What is a unit of electricity?

faq.q: Why do heating appliances use so much power?
faq.a: Making heat needs a lot of energy each second, so heaters and kettles have big power ratings.
asks: Why does a kettle use so much electricity?

facts: A typical electric kettle is rated at about 2–3 kW; an LED bulb at about 5–10 W.
